newsitem.title: IRAN: Three women among 13 election winners in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Three women among 13 election winners in Iran.

text.p: Winners were declared on Saturday in 13 by-elections for seats in Iran's 270-member parliament, with three women among the victors, officials said.
Officials said they expected to name winners on Sunday in the remaining nine of the 22 seats being contested because last year's results were annulled.
The initial results of Friday's voting showed victory for five centrists, three conservatives and five independents, officials said. Three of the winners were women, they added.

Results from last year's parliamentary polls in Iran's third largest city Isfahan and some other districts were annulled by the Guardian Council, a body of clerics and lawyers that oversees elections, because of alleged irregularities.

Local issues dominated the by-election campaigns, but there has been tension between conservatives and centrist backers of President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani over a screening process which decided who was allowed to run.
Screening committees set up by the Guardian Council approved 215 candidates from about twice as many contenders last month. Some later withdrew.
The council screens candidates for their belief in Islam and Iran's system of Islamic government, including the rule that the state is headed by a supreme spiritual leader.

Some political figures and newspapers criticised last year's annulments, particularly the one in Isfahan, saying they favoured conservatives who oppose Rafsanjani's reform policies and his centrist supporters.

Conservatives, led by parliamentary speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, kept their Majlis majority in last year's elections. But analysts said they face a strong minority coalition of pro-Rafsanjani centrists, radical Islamist intellectuals and labour groups.
The 22 new Majlis members' votes could be significant because of the small gap between parliament's two political blocs, analysts said.

Also at stake is momentum for presidential polls, due to be held in May or June, in which Rafsanjani is barred from running after serving two four-year terms. Nateq-Nouri appears to be the leading candidate.
